messages:
bryan: Hey team — noticed our staging connector (zendesk-integ) started returning 403s immediately after an API key rotation ~08:02 UTC. Occurred for all users, SSO tokens look valid but calls fail. Can someone help triage? :grimacing:

oliver: @bryan — thanks for flagging. Do you have a recent request/response snippet (headers + error body)? Also which rotation was this (Vault kv update or CI secrets push)?

bryan: Quick paste of response from the connector logs:```
2024-09-12T08:03:12Z ERROR http: upstream request failed status=403 body="{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\"}" headers={Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, X-Request-ID: rq_9f2b}
```
We rotated the Zendesk API key in Vault at 07:58, then kicked a CI job to deploy connector config at 08:00. Vault shows new version available.

maria: Can you run `kubectl describe pod <connector-pod>` and check env (envFrom/configMap) — common pattern: CI rendered old key into a configmap or k8s secret and the pod kept old value. Also check the sidecar (if present) for cached creds.

bryan: Running now — snippet:```
Name: zendesk-integ-5fdc8c6d6d-9p2l
Containers:
  app:
    Image: ghcr.io/redwood/zendesk-integ:stable
    Environment:
      ZENDESK_API_KEY: **** (from configmap/zendesk-config)
...\n```
The configmap was updated by CI at 08:00 but the value inside looks like the previous key (prefix `sk_live_old...`). Vault shows `sk_live_new...` at version 3.

julia: ok this smells like a CI rendering bug where it read an old vault token or secret alias. Two quick checks: 1) did the CI job actually pull latest Vault kv v2 version? check the job logs for the vault read call. 2) are there any rollout rollbacks (k8s event) that replaced the configmap after deploy?

support-bot: DeployBot: ci-build-5289 finished at 2024-09-12T08:00:12Z — applied configmap/ zendesk-config (hash: a1b2c3) -> rollout started.

oliver: @bryan can you grep CI logs for `vault kv get` or `vault kv get -field=api_key` around 07:58-08:00? Also check whether the Vault token used by CI expired and got rewrapped to an older cached secret.

bryan: Found CI lines:```
2024-09-12T07:58:43 vault kv get secret/staging/zendesk api_key=sk_live_newXYZ
2024-09-12T07:59:05 helm upgrade --set-file externalApiKey=<(echo $API_KEY) ...
2024-09-12T08:00:05 kubectl apply -f configmap.yaml
```
But theres also a separate job at 08:01 that says `helm rollback` (unexpected) with hash pointing to a prior release. Not sure who triggered it.

maria: aha — rollback would reapply the old configmap. Check `kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -n staging` for a `Rollback` event.

bryan: Events show `Deployment rollback triggered by user: ci-automation` at 08:01:12 and it reapplied release revision 27 (which contains the old key). I guess the automation retried and used cached helm chart values stored in artifact storage, not the freshly rendered one.

oliver: That matches: Vault had correct secret and CI read it, but a subsequent automated rollback re-deployed an older chart with the old key -> pods restarted with old key, resulting in 403 after some pods picked up the old key while others had new. The SSO tokens failing was a symptom because the connector uses the API key as a backend service auth and rejects token-exchange flows when the backend refuses.

julia: remediation steps: 1) Stop automated rollback job (ci-automation) temporarily. 2) Manually update configmap with `kubectl create configmap zendesk-config --from-literal=api_key=sk_live_newXYZ -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -` 3) Restart connector pods: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/zendesk-integ -n staging` 4) Purge connector in-memory key caches if any: POST /admin/cache/purge (call from bastion).

bryan: Executed steps 1-3. After restart, new pods show `ZENDESK_API_KEY=sk_live_newXYZ`. Called `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>" https://staging.zendesk-integ.local/health` and backend now returns 200.

support-bot: IncidentBot: ticket #INC-9271 created and linked to thread.

maria: Root cause writeup draft: CI automation (ci-automation) has a retry path that, on perceived deploy failure, executes a helm rollback using stored artifact values that did not include latest Vault-fetched secrets. This produced a window where rollout applied old configmap/secret, causing connector to present revoked/old API key to Zendesk -> 403s. Tokens weren't themselves invalid; the service call was rejected by the backend because of the old API key.

oliver: Next action items: - Add a preflight verification step in CI that validates deployed secret against Vault after apply (checksum compare) - Stop rollback autopilot until it validates artifact freshness - Add an alert if >30% of pods return 403/401 for an external integration for >2m - Run an incident postmortem and update runbook.

bryan: Confirmed staging is healthy now. Will watch production rotation later today and will require canary check. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

julia: I'll own the follow-ups. Filed RFC to change rollback behavior and added a CI guard to verify Vault version before allowing rollback.

maria: For the runbook please include the exact repro commands and the quick recovery snippet I ran (kubectl apply + rollout restart + cache purge).

bryan: copying final commands here for the runbook:```
# apply correct key
kubectl create configmap zendesk-config --from-literal=api_key=sk_live_newXYZ -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f - -n staging
# restart pods
kubectl rollout restart deployment/zendesk-integ -n staging
# purge in-memory cache (run from bastion)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://staging.zendesk-integ.local/admin/cache/purge
```

oliver: Great, closing thread once postmortem is posted. :white_check_mark:
